3.text: were distributed between these two groups of tributaries. The Maritime group

4.text: was much more important, because all the best peltries of American provenience

5.text: were brought by the traders of this group.

6.text: Regulations of Treskin. — Trade at the Anui fair was carried on more

7.text: or less uninterruptedly until 1811. In that year General Treskin, Governor

8.text: of Irkutsk, introduced a set of rules which were to regulate with the utmost

9.text: strictness trade with the Chukchee. These rules were put into force in 1812,

10.text: and observed, until 1869, when they were repealed by Maydell. Treskin,

11.text: even for his time, was famous for his cruelty and corruptness, and his career

12.text: terminated by his being officially prosecuted in court. Among his other qualities

13.text: was his constant desire to regulate strictly the whole course of life, which is

14.text: so characteristic of all the bureaucracy of the St. Petersburg period of Russian

15.text: history. The most essential feature of his rules and regulations was the fixed

16.text: table of prices for all the more expensive objects of sale brought to the fair;

17.text: such as beavers, all kinds of foxes, martens, and walrus-ivory, and, as the

18.text: Russian equivalent, tobacco, and often also kettles, iron, and copper. The staple

19.text: article of value offered for sale by the Chukchee was the red fox; and that

20.text: offered by the Russians, tobacco. Objects of minor value, such as reindeer-meat

21.text: and seal-thong, were sold at free prices in exchange for iron-work, sugar, etc.

22.text: In some years fawn-skins were included in the table, but for the most part

23.text: these were sold free. In some years Cossacks and the common citizens were

24.text: given the right to carry on some small traffic with the Chukchee to the

25.text: amount of one pud of tobacco, but only for the necessaries of life, such as

26.text: meat and clothing. In other years even that right was taken away.

27.text: The table of prices had to be established every year by deputies of

28.text: traders, in accord with the chief officer and the principal Chukchee traders;
